dev.readyCheck: the Home route renders; drive it with the Chrome DevTools MCP server and take_snapshot, which needs no image-input consent

gates.name: eslint
gates.caveat: eslint-plugin-boundaries fails open. A file under src/ that no element pattern in eslint.config.js classifies is simply unchecked, so the architectural rule passes vacuously on any directory shape the config does not name.

gates.name: prettier --check
gates.caveat: .prettierignore excludes .agents/vendor/ deliberately — layer A owns its own formatting and reflowing it here would break the vendored copy's sha check on every sync.

gates.name: vite build
gates.caveat: this is the only gate that checks the browser target. A top-level await passes typecheck and still fails the build against es2020 — which is why it is a gate and not a release step.

gates.name: playwright
gates.when: the change alters user-visible behaviour, real navigation, focus across a page load, or anything depending on real layout
gates.caveat: needs browsers installed: pnpm exec playwright install chromium.

gates.name: lighthouse
gates.when: performance or accessibility budgets are in scope
gates.caveat: exits 0 far more readily than it looks. Only the accessibility assertion is `error`; performance, best-practices and SEO are `warn`, and the performance category currently scores null because the pinned Lighthouse cannot trace against the installed Chrome. A category with no score is not a pass — read the assertion output, not the exit code.
